headline: Growing Community Screenshots Everything 'In Case Reality Gets Patched'
subheadline: Threadit group reaches 847,000 members convinced digital evidence may be only proof of 'original timeline'
summary: A Threadit community dedicated to screenshotting mundane content has grown exponentially, driven by users who believe reality may be retroactively edited.
content:
The Threadit community r/ScreenshotEverything has quietly grown into one of the platform's most active groups, united by a simple philosophy: nothing online is permanent, including the fundamental nature of existence.

"You ever see a meme and then a week later you can't find it anywhere?" wrote moderator TruthArchiver_847 in the community's pinned FAQ. "That's not just content being deleted. That's evidence of a patch."

The group, which reached 847,000 subscribers this morning, encourages members to screenshot everything they encounter online, from news articles to weather forecasts to mundane Chirper posts about someone's lunch.

"I screenshot every Gooble search result," explained user DigitalPrepper in a recent thread. "Two months ago I searched 'how many bones in human body' and it said 206. Searched again last week. Still 206. But I have the screenshot. If it ever changes, I'll know."

The community maintains an elaborate tagging system to organize their collective archive. Categories include "Potentially Mandela Effect," "Suspicious Edits," and the ominously titled "Reality Anchor Evidence."

Psychologist Dr. Eleanor Finch has studied the group for her upcoming paper on digital anxiety disorders.

"There's a genuine fear that the digital world, and by extension reality itself, is mutable," Dr. Finch explained. "These users aren't necessarily experiencing delusions. They're responding rationally to an environment where content genuinely does disappear, get edited, and change without notice. They've just extrapolated that anxiety to its logical extreme."

The community has produced some genuinely useful archives. When a local restaurant was accused of changing their menu prices retroactively, r/ScreenshotEverything produced 847 dated screenshots proving the price increase.

Not all members believe in literal reality patches. User SkepticalArchiver claims he just likes having receipts.

"I screenshot arguments," he wrote. "People delete their worst takes. Not if I screenshot them first."

The group's most active poster, AllEvidenceMatters, claims to have taken over 2 million screenshots in the past three years. When asked how they organize this archive, they simply responded: "I don't. That's future me's problem."

Threadit administrators have noted the group's storage footprint but have not taken action, stating the community violates no platform rules.
author: Cassandra Webb, Internet Culture
